title: Baharat Mushroom and Turkey Burgers
changes_from_base: Half the meat is replaced by finely chopped roasted mushrooms, and the mix is spiced with a home-ground baharat of black pepper, allspice, cumin, cinnamon and nutmeg plus plenty of fresh herbs; patties are seared, then finished in the oven. My own simple roasted mushroom mix stands in for the referenced base.
summary: Deeply savoury turkey burgers flavoured with umami-rich roasted mushrooms and warm baharat spice, finished in the oven until tender and juicy.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast mushrooms
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan). Toss 680 g finely chopped chestnut mushrooms with 30 ml olive oil and ½ tsp fine salt on a lined baking tray and roast for 25-30 minutes, stirring halfway through twice, until they have released their liquid and look dry and browned; set aside to cool.

steps.title: Baharat spice
steps.text: Grind 2 tbsp black peppercorns, 2 tbsp allspice berries and ½ tsp cumin seeds to a powder using a spice grinder. Stir in 1 tsp ground cinnamon and ½ tsp freshly grated nutmeg and store in a small jar.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a large bowl combine 450 g turkey mince, the cooled roasted mushrooms, ½ medium finely chopped onion, 2 finely grated garlic cloves, 15 g chopped flat-leaf parsley, 2 tbsp chopped mint or dill, 2 tbsp chopped coriander, 1 tsp fine salt, ¼ tsp cayenne pepper and 1 large egg. Mix very gently until just combined.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Divide the mixture into 6 equal portions and gently shape each into a patty. Set them on an oiled baking tray and chill for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp rapeseed or grapeseed oil in a large heavy frying pan over a medium-high heat and sear the patties for 4 minutes on each side, working in batches if necessary, until both sides are well browned.

steps.title: Finish in oven
steps.text: Transfer the seared patties to a lined baking tray and bake in a 220 °C oven (200 °C fan) for 7-8 minutes until the centre reaches 74 °C. Let them rest for 2 minutes before serving.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Arrange each patty in a split wholemeal bun with fresh lettuce leaves and sliced tomato.

tips: The roasted mushrooms can be made up to 3 days ahead and kept in the fridge, so you can shape and cook the burgers whenever you like.
Sear the patties in a heavy pan first for a golden crust, then finish them in the oven to cook them through gently without drying the centres.
Shape the patties ahead if convenient; they can wait in the fridge for several hours or be wrapped and frozen for up to 3 months.
storage: The cooled roasted mushrooms keep refrigerated for up to 3 days; uncooked patties freeze well for up to 3 months when wrapped individually. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
